name: Sharr Mountains National Park
blurb: Beech and pine forests, high pastures and the last Balkan lynx.

tip.title: Remove the wolves
tip.text: Wolves hunt deer, chamois, boar and voles. Set Gray wolf to -100% and watch the herbivores grow, then the forest and pasture plants they eat.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Summer light drives growth in the meadows and forests, but the growing season is short at altitude.
Mountain rain and cloud water feed the forests and the high pastures.
Forest and meadow soils hold the nutrients that plants take up.
Break down fallen leaves, dead wood and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
A broadleaf tree of the lower and middle forest slopes. Its nuts and leaves feed many forest animals.
A Balkan pine found in the upper forest belt of the Sharr range; its seeds and needles feed forest animals.

nodes.name: Mountain grasses
nodes.desc: Fescue grasses form part of the high pastures above the tree line, which are among the largest compact pastures in Europe.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A goat-antelope of steep rocky slopes. It grazes grasses and herbs in summer and eats conifer bark and needles in winter.
A small forest deer that browses in the woods and meadow edges of the range.
An omnivore of the forest that roots for nuts, plants and invertebrates.
A grass and herb eater of open ground; the Balkan lynx is known to hunt it.

nodes.name: Eurasian red squirrel
nodes.desc: A tree squirrel of the conifer and mixed forests, feeding on seeds and nuts.
A small forest rodent eating seeds, fruit and green plants; a common prey of many predators.
A rare rock-dwelling rodent of Balkan mountains, recorded on the Sharr slopes.
A flexible hunter and fruit eater that takes rodents, birds and eggs.
An omnivorous ground forager that eats rodents, amphibians, reptiles and plant foods.
A raptor that hunts small mammals, reptiles and birds over forest edges and meadows.
A large scavenger that feeds mainly on carrion; it is the most-recorded bird in the GBIF data for the area.
A Critically Endangered cat, with very few animals left. It hunts mainly roe deer, young chamois and hares.
A pack hunter of the range, taking deer, boar, chamois and smaller mammals.
An omnivore of the forests that eats plant foods, small mammals and carrion.

story: Sharr Mountains National Park covers 532.72 km2 of southern Kosovo on the northern Sharr Mountains. Declared in 1986 and re-established in 2012, it contains glacial lakes, alpine and periglacial landscapes, and numerous species of plants, mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibia, fish, and butterflies.
matters: The park falls entirely within the Balkan mixed forests terrestrial ecoregion of the Palearctic temperate broadleaf and mixed forests biome. It provides a home and habitat for diverse native wildlife and vegetation.
